task.title: Decision log and MVP success criteria
task.completionRule: Keep this task ready until every decision has an accountable owner, a decision deadline, and recorded evidence, and the V1 interview threshold is met.

decisions.question: Which video provider can meet the product, commercial, retention, region, and watermark requirements?

providerAssessment.classification: Video-provider selection is deferred. ARS-006A/006B separates MiniMax H3 open-weight licensing from its globally documented hosted API and keeps Wan2.2 TI2V-5B only as a benchmark candidate.
providerAssessment.currentNeed: No runtime provider is needed for the current PNG and deterministic motion-GIF stage. Revisit only after provider, commercial, budget, upload, delivery, safety, hardware, and region gates have recorded evidence.

candidates.resolution: H3-Base 768p; full 2K workflow is not fully open-source
candidates.hardwareFloor: Official SGLang deployment example uses 4 GPUs; per-GPU VRAM floor is not stated.

candidates.duration: not fixed by the official product documentation; frame-count based
candidates.audio: not documented as a native TI2V output
candidates.territoryEligibility: no South Korea exclusion identified in the official Apache-2.0 model materials
candidates.hardwareFloor: Official single-GPU TI2V-5B example requires at least 24GB VRAM with offload, dtype conversion, and T5 on CPU.
unknowns: data use and retention for any hosted path

decisionInputs.summary: Public site first; commercially scale only when video production and distribution show viability.

researchContext.summary: Corrected official-source ARS-006A/006B review: MiniMax H3 open weights require a formal license for South Korean deployment, while MiniMax documents the safeguarded MiniMax-H3 /v2 hosted API as globally available but not yet approved for product integration. Wan2.2 TI2V-5B remains an unselected Apache-2.0 benchmark candidate requiring at least 24GB VRAM in the official single-GPU example.
Sora 2 and Sora 2 Pro support 16- and 20-second generations; Sora 2 Pro supports 1080x1920 output. Copyrighted characters/music and real people are restricted.
The published Sora 2 Pro 1080p rate is US$0.70 per second, making a 16-second attempt approximately US$11.20 before storage and operations.

Provider eligibility and original, non-identifying credentialed spike evidence.
Private owned storage, delivery, webhook, trim/QC, caption, thumbnail, and manifest readiness.
requiredEvidence: Provider capability and price comparison for the original 15-second vertical brief.
Written commercial, data-use, retention/deletion, and region confirmation.
Credentialed spike result using only an original, non-identifying reference.
decisions.releaseImpact: Blocks any switch from the mock provider and all real video delivery.

decisions.question: What are the per-user generation, retry, and payment limits?

decisionInputs.summary: Confirmed per-user limit: maximum 5 generation submissions per day and 3 retry submissions per hour.

retryPolicy.dailyQuotaTreatment: Each retry submission counts against the per-user maximum of five generation submissions per day.
retryPolicy.enforcementStatus: documentation_only: no user identity, persistence, or retry endpoint exists in the local MVP

commercialStageProposal.paymentModel: Prepaid render credits through a hosted checkout; do not start with a subscription during public validation.
commercialStageProposal.paymentProviderCandidate: PortOne V2 with a Toss Payments channel for Korean-won checkout.
commercialStageProposal.costCircuitBreaker: Enforce the selected provider-wide monthly cap and user quota server-side before creating a render job.
commercialStageProposal.limitation: This is a research-backed candidate, not a payment contract, integration, or commercial approval.

researchContext.summary: PortOne documents server-side billing-key payment requests and scheduled billing flows.
Toss Payments documents a hosted payment widget with multiple payment methods.

pendingQuestions: User-selected numeric monthly provider spend cap and the currency/approval owner.
Commercial billing contract, fees, tax/refund policy, and payment terms.
Server-side idempotency, payment verification, credit ledger, quota, and circuit-breaker design.
requiredEvidence: Cost model based on verified provider pricing and expected retry rate.
Approved spending cap, retry policy, and user-facing limit proposal.
decisions.releaseImpact: Blocks quota, retry, payment, and cost-control implementation.

decisions.question: Which languages are supported, and what are the TTS, caption, and rights-review criteria?

decisionInputs.summary: Korean-only MVP; defer TTS to the commercial stage; request Japanese, English, and Chinese captions through STT.

decisions.clarification: STT transcribes speech. Japanese, English, and Chinese captions for Korean speech require a separate translation step (or a multilingual source recording), plus quality and rights criteria.
pendingQuestions: Whether translated Japanese, English, and Chinese captions are included in the MVP or deferred after Korean-caption validation.
Translation provider, retention/data-use terms, quality threshold, and human correction flow.
Caption accessibility, export, and deletion requirements for every supported language.
requiredEvidence: Language-quality and accessibility requirements for the MVP.
Rights and consent review for every proposed voice, caption, and translation path.
decisions.releaseImpact: Blocks multilingual generation, caption, and TTS release claims.

decisions.question: How are licensed B2B requests verified, escalated, and assigned legal responsibility?

decisionInputs.summary: Asked whether B2B licensing means anime copyright and whether a derivative work requires rights.

researchContext.summary: Copyright Act Article 5 protects derivative works independently but does not affect the original author's rights.
Korea Copyright Commission states that an unauthorized derivative work can still infringe the original right holder's derivative-work right.

decisions.policyPosition: A B2B licence route is not an automatic anime or derivative-work permission. The public MVP continues to block or send explicit copyrighted-character, copied-scene, and licence-claim requests to review; this note is not legal advice or licence approval.
pendingQuestions: Authorized legal review of the exact source work, territory, media, duration, distribution, modification, AI/provider, attribution, and sublicensing rights.
Rights-holder or authorized licensee verification, signed licence scope, and escalation/record-retention process.
requiredEvidence: Approved licence-proof review and escalation procedure.
Named legal owner and record-retention/deletion policy.
decisions.releaseImpact: Blocks licensed-request automation and any claim that a licence assertion grants permission.

v1Interview.completionRule: Each anonymized record must show a participant independently reached request-to-storyboard confirmation without production-media collection.

automationBoundary: This file and its checker record missing external evidence. They do not approve rights, safety, privacy, provider terms, or production release.
